screening_decisions.reason: Animal study (mice) not human; tests heparanase not hyaluronic acid; not a randomized controlled trial in women undergoing ART.
Animal study (bovine/cattle embryos) not human; while it tests HA, the population criterion is not met.
Matched controlled study, not a randomized controlled trial; the selection criteria require truly randomised controlled trials.
Randomized clinical trial in women undergoing IVF; compares HA-enriched embryo transfer medium vs routine medium without HA; meets all selection criteria.
Prospective randomized controlled trial in women undergoing IVF; compares hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (HETM) vs conventional transfer medium; meets all selection criteria.

Primary intervention is freezing protocol (temperature/cooling rate), not embryo transfer media with adherence compounds; HA is mentioned only as part of culture media, not the comparison of interest.
Basic science animal study (mouse uteri); examines hyaluronate biosynthesis mechanisms, not a clinical trial of embryo transfer media.

Prospective randomized clinical trial in women undergoing IVF/ICSI; compares EmbryoGlue (contains HA) vs no treatment before transfer; meets selection criteria for adherence compound in embryo transfer media.
Observational study examining CD44 expression; no intervention or comparison of embryo transfer media; not a randomized controlled trial.
Case-control study, not a randomized controlled trial; also tests fibrin sealant, not hyaluronic acid/adherence compounds.
Preliminary case series (n=38), not a randomized controlled trial; tests fibrin sealant, not hyaluronic acid.
Review article summarizing existing studies; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Cell culture study (chick heart fibroblasts, 3T3 cells); basic science research, not a clinical trial in humans.
Cochrane review protocol/article; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Randomized trial but compares albumin sources (HSA vs rHA), not adherence compounds like hyaluronic acid; does not meet intervention criterion.
Retrospective observational study; not a randomized controlled trial; does not test adherence compounds.
Observational study (prospective comparison), not a randomized controlled trial; selection criteria require truly randomised controlled trials.
Animal study (bovine embryos); not a clinical trial in women undergoing ART.
Prospective randomized double-blind study in women undergoing IVF; compares HA-supplemented transfer medium vs synthetic serum substitute; meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial but compares G5 vs HTF culture media, neither of which involves adherence compounds like hyaluronic acid; does not meet intervention criterion.

This is a methodological review examining statistical errors in subfertility trials, not an RCT testing adherence compounds in embryo transfer media. It reviews 39 trials published in 2001 but does not itself test any intervention.

This study compares two sequential embryo CULTURE media (G1.2-G2.2 vs GIII series), not embryo TRANSFER media. Additionally, it uses quasi-randomization (alternating weekdays) rather than true randomization, and does not specifically test adherence compounds like hyaluronic acid.

While this is a randomized trial testing an adherence compound (fibrin sealant) in embryo transfer, the review specifically focuses on hyaluronic acid as the adherence compound of interest. Fibrin sealant is a different type of adherence compound not within the scope of this review.

This study tests EmbryoGlue (hyaluronan-enriched medium) but is explicitly described as a 'prospective case-control study', not a randomized controlled trial. The selection criteria require truly randomized controlled trials only.

This study compares two embryo CULTURE media (GIII series vs ISM), not embryo TRANSFER media. While sibling oocytes were randomly assigned, the intervention is culture medium composition, not transfer medium with adherence compounds.
This is an animal study conducted in mice, not humans. The review focuses on assisted reproductive technologies in women undergoing ART. Animal studies do not meet the population criteria.
This is a basic science study examining gene expression (HYAL2, HAS genes) in bovine embryos. It is not a clinical trial in humans and does not test embryo transfer media with adherence compounds.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing hyaluronic acid versus albumin in human embryo transfer medium. 60 women were randomly allocated to two groups: treatment group received hyaluronic acid-supplemented transfer medium, control group received albumin-containing medium. This meets all selection criteria: true RCT, human participants, comparing HA-containing transfer medium to control.

This randomized trial compares single versus double blastocyst transfer, not embryo transfer media with adherence compounds. The intervention is the number of embryos transferred, not the composition of the transfer medium.

This appears to be a brief abstract/report stating that EmbryoGlue did not significantly improve outcomes. There is insufficient information to confirm this is a true RCT, and the abstract suggests future RCTs are needed, implying this may not be one. Without confirmation of randomization, must exclude.

This is an observational study examining hyaluronan distribution in human endometrium across the menstrual cycle using histochemical localization. It is not an interventional study and does not test embryo transfer media.

While this is a randomized trial testing hyaluronan in transfer media, it compares LOW concentration HA versus HIGH concentration HA. Both groups receive hyaluronan, so there is no control group with NO or LOW adherence compound concentration. The selection criteria require comparison to media with no or low adherence compound concentrations.

This is a prospective randomized clinical trial with 581 IVF-ET cycles comparing hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (n=290) to conventional embryo transfer medium without hyaluronan (n=291). This meets all selection criteria: true RCT, human participants, comparing HA-containing transfer medium to control medium without HA.

This is a laboratory study examining CD44 isoform expression in human endometrium using immunofluorescence and RT-PCR. It is not a clinical trial and does not test embryo transfer media with adherence compounds.

This is a randomized trial with 314 patients comparing hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (0.5 mg/ml hyaluronan) to control medium containing NO hyaluronan. Patients were randomized on the day of ET. This meets all selection criteria: true RCT, human participants with history of multiple implantation failures, comparing HA-containing transfer medium to control without HA.

This multicenter randomized study examines increased viscosity in transfer medium, but the abstract does not specify that hyaluronic acid or another adherence compound was used to increase viscosity. The intervention is unclear from the abstract, and it may not be testing adherence compounds specifically.

This randomized trial tests hyaluronidase enzyme concentration for OOCYTE DENUDATION, not embryo transfer media. Hyaluronidase is an enzyme that BREAKS DOWN hyaluronic acid (opposite function of adherence compounds), and the intervention occurs at a different stage of the ART process.
